name: Lamb chop and pineapple diet

lead: The lamb chop and pineapple diet was an American high-protein fad diet of the 1920s. Silent-film actress Nita Naldi said in 1924 that it helped her lose twenty pounds, and other Hollywood figures followed, as part of a period push for slimmer figures.

Promoters said lamb gave protein for strength and pineapple gave sugar for energy, with the fruit's acid breaking down leftover fat. Weight loss reported on it is attributed by commentators to very low calorie intake, and Naldi later described dizziness and hunger.

paras: Meals were built from grilled lamb chops with pineapple slices. One account of Naldi's version lists black coffee for breakfast, a single broiled chop with pineapple at lunch and two chops with two slices of pineapple at dinner.
Nutritionists advised against it because an unbalanced plan does not supply the nutrients the body needs. Naldi reportedly fell ill for weeks and quit after dizziness and hunger.

chain: Meals limited to lamb chops and pineapple
angle.text: People followed it to slim down. Commentators attribute the weight lost to the small amount of food eaten rather than to pineapple acid.

lead: The lamb chop and pineapple diet was an American high-protein fad diet popular in the 1920s, in which meals consisted of lamb chops and pineapple [1]. It belongs to the period's push for thinness, and its aim was the same one as today's cutting diets: a slimmer figure [1][2].

The actress Nita Naldi adopted and promoted it in 1924, saying she lost twenty pounds [1][2]. Promoters held that lamb supplied protein, pineapple supplied sugar, and the fruit's acid absorbed leftover fat; the mechanism was never explained [1][2].

paras: The plan limited eating to grilled lamb chops and pineapple [1]. One account of Naldi's regimen gives black coffee for breakfast, one broiled chop with pineapple for lunch, and two chops with two slices of pineapple for dinner [2]. No one is credited with inventing it [2].

Naldi's 1924 statement that she had lost over twenty pounds is reported to have encouraged many others to try it, and other Hollywood celebrities adopted it [1][2]. The history is covered in Heather Addison's book on Hollywood and physical culture [2]. The press also scrutinised Naldi's supposed eating habits [2].

Promoters said pineapple's acid neutralised or broke down fat from the lamb; the article on the diet notes this mechanism was never explained [1][2]. Commentators say weight loss came mainly from severe calorie restriction, and that the diet is low in calories and nutrients [2]. Nutritionists advised against it as an unbalanced fad diet [1]. Naldi later described near-fainting and dizziness [2].
Fad diets in general are described as short-term and often followed by weight regain, with highly restrictive versions linked to malnutrition if continued [3].

timeline.event: Nita Naldi promotes the diet, reporting a twenty-pound loss [1]
